source.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

pt.L: A palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a mim, dizendo:
pt.B: A palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a mim:
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} me deu esta mensagem:

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me: the message about Gog
decisions.reason: Chapters 38-39 are one long message against Gog, a ruler from the far north who leads many nations against Israel after it has been restored and lives in peace. The LORD defeats him on the mountains of Israel, so that all the nations know him. The passage looks to "the latter years" (verse 8) and is unlike the oracles against known nations in chapters 25-32.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying: (L); The word of the LORD came to me: (B); The LORD gave me this message: (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Jeremiah and Ezekiel. What follows is the LORD's message, which takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

source.text: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם שִׂ֤ים פָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶל־גּוֹג֙ אֶ֣רֶץ הַמָּג֔וֹג נְשִׂ֕יא רֹ֖אשׁ מֶ֣שֶׁךְ וְתֻבָ֑ל וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Son of man, set your face toward Gog, [of] the land of Magog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him,

en.L: Son of man, set your face toward Gog, [of] the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him,
en.B: Son of man, turn to face Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, from the land of Magog, and prophesy against him.
en.R: Son of man, turn toward Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, from the land of Magog. Prophesy against him.

pt.L: Filho do homem, põe o teu rosto em direção a Gogue, [da] terra de Magogue, o príncipe supremo de Meseque e Tubal, e profetiza contra ele,
pt.B: Filho do homem, volta o rosto para Gogue, o príncipe supremo de Meseque e Tubal, da terra de Magogue, e profetiza contra ele.
pt.R: Filho do homem, vira-te para Gogue, o príncipe supremo de Meseque e Tubal, da terra de Magogue. Profetiza contra ele.

decisions.choice: the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal: the word *rosh* as "chief"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew *nesi' rosh meshekh wetuval* can be read in two ways. *Rosh* is the ordinary word for "head", and joined to *nasi'* ("prince") it means "chief prince", the head ruler over Meshech and Tubal; this reading is followed here. The Septuagint and some later translations took *Rosh* as a name, "the prince of Rosh, Meshech and Tubal". No people called Rosh is known in the Bible or in the records of the ancient Near East from this time, which makes the name reading less likely, but it cannot be ruled out. In either case Rosh is not Russia: the name Russia comes from the Rus', a people of the early Middle Ages, more than fifteen hundred years after Ezekiel, and the likeness of the two names is a coincidence. In the same way, Meshech and Tubal are not Moscow and Tobolsk.

decisions.choice: Gog, the land of Magog, Meshech and Tubal: a ruler and peoples of the far north
decisions.reason: Meshech and Tubal were peoples of eastern Asia Minor (central Turkey today), named among the sons of Japheth in Genesis 10:2 together with Magog, and known from Assyrian records as Mushku and Tabal; Ezekiel names them as traders and warriors in 27:13 and 32:26. Magog is not otherwise known as a place. Gog is not a known king of Ezekiel's time; some have linked the name with Gyges, a king of Lydia in the seventh century BC, but this is uncertain. In Ezekiel he stands for the last great enemy of God's people.

decisions.choice: Gog and Magog: Revelation 20:8
decisions.reason: Revelation 20:8 takes up the names, speaking of "the nations that are at the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog", gathered for the last battle against "the camp of the saints and the beloved city", until fire comes down from heaven and devours them (Revelation 20:9; compare 38:22; 39:6). There Gog and Magog are both names for the nations, not a ruler and his land.

decisions.choice: the chief prince (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase in Ezekiel at every level, with the other reading in the footnote (m1). "Prince" is *nasi'* (see 34:24); here, of a foreign ruler, Readable keeps "prince" too, so that the set phrase is the same at every level. *Sim panekha* follows the wording set at 6:2. Literal and Readable mark the land as Gog's with "[of]" and "from".

decisions.choice: Gogue, Magogue; o príncipe supremo de Meseque e Tubal (every level)
alternatives: o príncipe de Rôs, Meseque e Tubal
decisions.reason: For the whole passage (38-39): the names in the forms Revelation 20:8 uses in Portuguese ("Gogue e Magogue", m3), with "-gue" for the hard "g". Rosh is read with nasi' as "chief prince" (m1), so Portuguese says "príncipe supremo" at every level, as the English keeps "chief prince", with "príncipe" also at Readable for a foreign ruler.

decisions.choice: põe o teu rosto em direção a (L); volta o rosto para (B); vira-te para (R)
decisions.reason: The gesture of setting one's face toward those addressed, in the wording 6:2 sets for the book in Portuguese, with God's "tu" to the prophet.

source.text: וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הִנְנִ֤י אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ גּ֔וֹג נְשִׂ֕יא רֹ֖אשׁ מֶ֥שֶׁךְ וְתֻבָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: and say: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Here I [am] against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.

en.L: and say, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am] against you, Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
en.B: Say, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am against you, Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
en.R: Tell him, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Gog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, I am against you.

pt.L: e dize: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Eis que eu [estou] contra ti, Gogue, príncipe supremo de Meseque e Tubal.
pt.B: Dize: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Estou contra ti, Gogue, príncipe supremo de Meseque e Tubal.
pt.R: Dize a ele: É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz: Gogue, príncipe supremo de Meseque e Tubal, eu estou contra ti.

decisions.choice: look, I am against you: the LORD's judgment announced
the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, as in verse 2
decisions.reason: The wording set for the phrase at every level (see verse 2). The formula follows 2:4.

decisions.choice: ti, te, teu (tu) to Gog
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks to Gog with "tu", as to the kings and cities of the other oracles (the Ezekiel notes); it is the prophetic address of God to one hearer, not familiarity.

source.text: וְשׁ֣וֹבַבְתִּ֔יךָ וְנָתַתִּ֥י חַחִ֖ים בִּלְחָיֶ֑יךָ וְהוֹצֵאתִי֩ אוֹתְךָ֨וְאֶת־כָּל־חֵילֶ֜ךָ סוּסִ֣ים וּפָרָשִׁ֗ים לְבֻשֵׁ֤י מִכְלוֹל֙ כֻּלָּ֔ם קָהָ֥ל רָב֙ צִנָּ֣ה וּמָגֵ֔ן תֹּפְשֵׂ֥י חֲרָב֖וֹת כֻּלָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will turn you around and put hooks in your jaws, and bring you out, and all your army, horses and horsemen, clothed in full armor all of them, a great company [with] large shield and small shield, wielding swords, all of them:

en.L: And I will turn you around and put hooks in your jaws, and I will bring you out, and all your army, horses and horsemen, clothed in full splendor all of them, a great assembly [with] large shield and small shield, wielding swords all of them:
en.B: I will turn you around, put hooks in your jaws and lead you out with all your army, your horses and your horsemen, every one of them fully armed, a great company with shields large and small, all of them carrying swords.
en.R: I will turn you around and put hooks in your jaws and pull you out with your whole army. There will be horses and horsemen, all wearing full armor, a huge army. All of them will carry large and small shields and swords.

pt.L: E te farei dar a volta, e porei ganchos nas tuas queixadas, e te farei sair, e todo o teu exército, cavalos e cavaleiros, vestidos com toda a perfeição, todos eles, uma grande multidão [com] escudo grande e escudo pequeno, empunhando espadas, todos eles:
pt.B: Eu te farei dar a volta, porei ganchos nas tuas queixadas e te farei sair com todo o teu exército, os teus cavalos e os teus cavaleiros, todos eles completamente armados, uma grande multidão com escudos grandes e pequenos, todos empunhando espadas.
pt.R: Vou te fazer dar a volta, vou pôr ganchos nas tuas queixadas e vou te arrastar para fora com todo o teu exército. Haverá cavalos e cavaleiros, todos com armadura completa, um exército enorme. Todos eles vão carregar escudos grandes e pequenos e espadas.

decisions.choice: I will put hooks in your jaws: I will lead you like a captured animal
decisions.reason: The picture is of a wild animal, or a captive, led by a hook through the jaw (19:4; 29:4; 2 Kings 19:28). Gog thinks he comes by his own plan (verse 10), but the LORD is leading him.

decisions.choice: I will bring you out: the LORD brings Gog against Israel
decisions.reason: The LORD is in control of the invader from the start. He brings Gog to show his holiness through his defeat (verse 16).

decisions.choice: large shield and small shield
decisions.reason: The *tsinnah* was a large shield that covered the body; the *magen* a smaller round shield. Together they mean a fully armed force.

decisions.choice: all of them (L, B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "all of them" for the size of the army. The list runs on into verses 5-6.

source.text: פָּרַ֛ס כּ֥וּשׁ וּפ֖וּט אִתָּ֑ם כֻּלָּ֖ם מָגֵ֥ן וְכוֹבָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: Persia, Cush and Put with them, all of them [with] shield and helmet;

en.L: Persia, Cush and Put with them, all of them [with] small shield and helmet;
en.B: Persia, Cush and Put are with them, all with shield and helmet.
en.R: Soldiers from Persia, Cush and Put will be with them. All of them will have shields and helmets.

pt.L: a Pérsia, Cuxe e Pute com eles, todos eles [com] escudo pequeno e capacete;
pt.B: a Pérsia, Cuxe e Pute estão com eles, todos com escudo e capacete.
pt.R: Soldados da Pérsia, de Cuxe e de Pute estarão com eles. Todos eles vão ter escudos e capacetes.

decisions.choice: Persia, Cush and Put: peoples from the east and the far south
decisions.reason: Persia lay east of Babylonia; Cush was the land south of Egypt, on the upper Nile (Sudan today); Put is usually placed in Libya, west of Egypt. With the northern peoples of verses 2 and 6, Gog's army comes from the ends of the known world.

decisions.choice: Soldiers from (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says that the names stand for soldiers from these lands.

decisions.choice: a Pérsia, Cuxe, Pute
decisions.reason: The names of the peoples as Brazilian Bibles spell them (m1), without putting today's countries in place of "Cuxe" and "Pute", as the English keeps the names.

source.text: גֹּ֚מֶר וְכָל־אֲגַפֶּ֔יהָ בֵּ֚ית תּֽוֹגַרְמָ֔ה יַרְכְּתֵ֥י צָפ֖וֹן וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲגַפָּ֑יו עַמִּ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים אִתָּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Gomer and all its troops, Beth-togarmah, the remotest parts of the north, and all its troops — many peoples with you.

en.L: Gomer and all its troops, Beth-togarmah [from] the remotest parts of the north and all its troops, many peoples [are] with you.
en.B: Gomer with all its troops, and Beth-togarmah from the farthest north with all its troops. Many peoples are with you.
en.R: Gomer will come with all its soldiers, and Beth-togarmah from the far north with all its soldiers. Many nations will come with you.

pt.L: Gomer e todas as suas tropas, Bete-Togarma, [dos] confins do norte, e todas as suas tropas, muitos povos [estão] contigo.
pt.B: Gomer com todas as suas tropas e Bete-Togarma, do extremo norte, com todas as suas tropas. Muitos povos estão contigo.
pt.R: Gomer virá com todos os seus soldados, e Bete-Togarma, do extremo norte, com todos os seus soldados. Muitas nações virão contigo.

decisions.choice: Gomer and Beth-togarmah: peoples north of the Black Sea and in eastern Asia Minor
decisions.reason: Gomer and Togarmah are named with Magog, Meshech and Tubal among the descendants of Japheth (Genesis 10:2-3). Gomer is usually identified with the Cimmerians, a people from north of the Black Sea who invaded Asia Minor; Beth-togarmah ("house of Togarmah") with a region in eastern Asia Minor, the Til-garimmu of Assyrian records (27:14).

decisions.choice: the remotest parts of the north: the far north
decisions.reason: The north was the direction from which invaders came (Jeremiah 1:14; 6:22). The phrase is used again in verse 15 and 39:2.

decisions.choice: Beth-togarmah (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the house of Togarmah". Each level keeps it as a place name, Beth-togarmah, as the published books do with similar names. Literal brackets "from" and "are".

decisions.choice: Bete-Togarma
decisions.reason: As the English keeps "Beth-togarmah" as one place name, Portuguese writes "Bete-Togarma", with "Bete" as in "Betel" and "Belém".

source.text: הִכֹּן֙ וְהָכֵ֣ן לְךָ֔ אַתָּ֕ה וְכָל־קְהָלֶ֖ךָ הַנִּקְהָלִ֣ים עָלֶ֑יךָ וְהָיִ֥יתָ לָהֶ֖ם לְמִשְׁמָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Be ready, and prepare yourself, you and all your company that are assembled about you, and be a guard for them.

en.L: Be ready, and prepare yourself, you and all your company that are assembled around you, and be a guard for them.
en.B: Get ready and be prepared, you and all the forces gathered around you, and take command of them.
en.R: Get ready! Be prepared, you and all the armies gathered around you. You will be their commander.

pt.L: Prepara-te, e apronta-te, tu e toda a tua multidão que está reunida ao teu redor, e sê para eles uma guarda.
pt.B: Prepara-te e fica pronto, tu e todas as tropas reunidas ao teu redor, e assume o comando delas.
pt.R: Prepara-te! Fica pronto, tu e todos os exércitos reunidos ao teu redor. Tu vais ser o comandante deles.

decisions.choice: be ready and prepare: a call to arms, perhaps in mockery
decisions.reason: The doubled command, using the same verb twice, sounds like the call to an army, but it may also be ironic: Gog gets ready for a battle the LORD has already decided.

decisions.choice: a guard for them: their commander
decisions.reason: The word means a guard or watch. It may mean that Gog is to stand guard over them, or to be the one they obey. The Septuagint reads "be for me a guard".

decisions.choice: take command of them (B); You will be their commander (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the more likely sense (m2).

source.text: מִיָּמִ֣ים רַבִּים֮ תִּפָּקֵד֒ בְּאַחֲרִ֨ית הַשָּׁנִ֜ים תָּב֣וֹא׀אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ׀מְשׁוֹבֶ֣בֶת מֵחֶ֗רֶב מְקֻבֶּ֨צֶת֙ מֵעַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים עַ֚ל הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־הָי֥וּ לְחָרְבָּ֖ה תָּמִ֑יד וְהִיא֙ מֵעַמִּ֣ים הוּצָ֔אָה וְיָשְׁב֥וּ לָבֶ֖טַח כֻּלָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: After many days you will be mustered; in the latter years you will come to a land restored from [the] sword, gathered from many peoples, on [the] mountains of Israel, which had been a continual waste; and it was brought out from the peoples, and they dwell securely, all of them.

en.L: After many days you will be summoned; in the latter years you will come into a land restored from the sword, [whose people were] gathered from many peoples onto the mountains of Israel, which had been a continual waste; its people were brought out from the peoples, and they are dwelling securely, all of them.
en.B: After many days you will be called up. In the latter years you will invade a land that has recovered from war, whose people have been brought together out of many nations onto the mountains of Israel, which had lain in ruins for a long time. They were brought out from the nations, and now they all live in safety.
en.R: After a long time you will be called to war. In the years to come you will attack a land that has recovered from war. Its people were brought back from many nations to the mountains of Israel, which had been empty and ruined for a long time. Now they all live in safety.

pt.L: Depois de muitos dias serás convocado; no fim dos anos virás a uma terra restaurada da espada, [cujo povo foi] reunido de muitos povos sobre os montes de Israel, que haviam sido uma desolação contínua; o seu povo foi tirado dos povos, e eles habitam em segurança, todos eles.
pt.B: Depois de muitos dias serás chamado às armas. Nos últimos anos invadirás uma terra que se recuperou da guerra, cujo povo foi reunido de muitas nações sobre os montes de Israel, que por muito tempo estiveram em ruínas. Eles foram tirados do meio das nações, e agora todos vivem em segurança.
pt.R: Depois de muito tempo, tu serás chamado para a guerra. Nos anos que virão, vais atacar uma terra que se recuperou da guerra. O seu povo foi trazido de volta de muitas nações para os montes de Israel, que por muito tempo ficaram vazios e em ruínas. Agora todos eles vivem em segurança.

decisions.choice: the latter years: a time still in the future
decisions.reason: The phrase, like "the latter days" in verse 16, points to a time far ahead, after Israel has been restored to its land (chapters 34-37). It need not mean the very end of history, but it is the future beyond the prophet's own day (compare Isaiah 2:2; Daniel 10:14).

decisions.choice: you will be mustered: you will be summoned
decisions.reason: The verb *paqad* can mean to muster an army, to call up, or to punish. Here Gog is called up for the battle, and it may also hint at his punishment.

decisions.choice: restored from the sword: recovered from war
decisions.reason: The land has come back from the destruction of war, and its people have returned from exile.

decisions.choice: [whose people were] (L)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words English needs to say who was gathered.

source.text: וְעָלִ֨יתָ֙ כַּשֹּׁאָ֣ה תָב֔וֹא כֶּעָנָ֛ן לְכַסּ֥וֹת הָאָ֖רֶץ תִּֽהְיֶ֑ה אַתָּה֙ וְכָל־אֲגַפֶּ֔יךָ וְעַמִּ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים אוֹתָֽךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you will go up like a storm; you will come like a cloud to cover the land, you and all your troops and many peoples with you.

en.L: And you will go up; like a storm you will come; like a cloud to cover the land you will be, you and all your troops and many peoples with you.
en.B: You will advance like a storm and come like a cloud covering the land, you and all your troops and the many peoples with you.
en.R: You will come like a storm. You and all your soldiers and many nations with you will cover the land like a cloud.

pt.L: E subirás; como uma tempestade virás; como uma nuvem para cobrir a terra serás, tu e todas as tuas tropas e muitos povos contigo.
pt.B: Avançarás como uma tempestade e virás como uma nuvem que cobre a terra, tu e todas as tuas tropas e os muitos povos que estão contigo.
pt.R: Tu virás como uma tempestade. Tu, todos os teus soldados e muitas nações contigo vão cobrir a terra como uma nuvem.

decisions.choice: like a storm, like a cloud covering the land: a vast, overwhelming army
decisions.reason: The pictures describe an army so large that it fills the land like storm clouds (Jeremiah 4:13). The word for storm may mean the noise of a storm, a crash of destruction.

decisions.choice: you will go up; you will come (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the two verbs of the Hebrew; Balanced joins them.

source.text: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה וְהָיָ֣ה׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יַעֲל֤וּ דְבָרִים֙ עַל־לְבָבֶ֔ךָ וְחָשַׁבְתָּ֖ מַחֲשֶׁ֥בֶת רָעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: And it will be on that day that words will come up on your heart, and you will devise an evil plan.

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: On that day words will rise up in your heart, and you will devise an evil scheme.
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: On that day thoughts will rise in your mind, and you will make a wicked plan.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: At that time you will start thinking about doing something evil. You will make an evil plan.

pt.L: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Naquele dia subirão palavras ao teu coração, e tramarás um plano maligno.
pt.B: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Naquele dia surgirão pensamentos na tua mente, e farás um plano perverso.
pt.R: É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz: Naquele tempo, tu vais começar a pensar em fazer o mal. Vais fazer um plano perverso.

decisions.choice: you will devise an evil plan: Gog's own choice
decisions.reason: The LORD brings Gog (verse 4), yet Gog acts by his own evil will. Both are true at once, as with Assyria in Isaiah 10:5-7 and the cross in Acts 2:23.

decisions.choice: words will come up on your heart: thoughts will come into your mind
decisions.reason: In Hebrew the heart is the seat of thought (see 11:19).

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4.

source.text: וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ אֶֽעֱלֶה֙ עַל־אֶ֣רֶץ פְּרָז֔וֹת אָבוֹא֙ הַשֹּׁ֣קְטִ֔ים יֹשְׁבֵ֖י לָבֶ֑טַח כֻּלָּ֗ם יֹֽשְׁבִים֙ בְּאֵ֣ין חוֹמָ֔ה וּבְרִ֥יחַ וּדְלָתַ֖יִם אֵ֥ין לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will say, I will go up against a land of open villages; I will come on the quiet [people], dwelling securely, all of them dwelling without walls, and bars and gates they have none,

en.L: And you will say, "I will go up against a land of open villages; I will go to those who are at peace, who live securely, all of them living without walls, and having neither bars nor gates,"
en.B: You will say, "I will attack a land of unwalled villages. I will come against a peaceful people living in safety, all of them living without walls, with no bars or gates,"
en.R: You will say, "I will attack a land where the villages have no walls. The people there live in peace and feel safe. None of their towns have walls or gates with bars."

pt.L: E dirás: "Subirei contra uma terra de aldeias abertas; irei até os que estão tranquilos, que habitam em segurança, todos eles habitando sem muros, e não tendo trancas nem portas",
pt.B: Dirás: "Atacarei uma terra de aldeias sem muros. Irei contra um povo tranquilo, que vive em segurança, todos morando sem muros, sem trancas e sem portas",
pt.R: Tu vais dizer: "Vou atacar uma terra onde as aldeias não têm muros. O povo de lá vive em paz e se sente seguro. Nenhuma das suas cidades tem muros nem portas com trancas."

decisions.choice: unwalled villages; walls, bars and gates: a defenseless land
decisions.reason: Ancient towns were defended by walls and by gates barred at night (Deuteronomy 3:5). A land of open villages could not hold off an army. Israel's safety is the LORD, not walls (Zechariah 2:8-9).

decisions.choice: double quotation marks for Gog's words
decisions.reason: Gog's thoughts are quoted as speech inside the LORD's message, so they take double quotation marks. The sentence runs on into verse 12.

source.text: לִשְׁלֹ֥ל שָׁלָ֖ל וְלָבֹ֣ז בַּ֑ז לְהָשִׁ֨יב יָדְךָ֜ עַל־חֳרָב֣וֹת נוֹשָׁבֹ֗ת וְאֶל־עַם֙ מְאֻסָּ֣ף מִגּוֹיִ֔ם עֹשֶׂה֙ מִקְנֶ֣ה וְקִנְיָ֔ן יֹשְׁבֵ֖י עַל־טַבּ֥וּר הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: to plunder plunder and to seize spoil, to turn your hand against waste places [now] inhabited, and against a people gathered from [the] nations, acquiring livestock and goods, who dwell at [the] navel of the earth.

en.L: to take plunder and to seize spoil, to turn your hand against the ruins [now] inhabited, and against a people gathered out of the nations, acquiring cattle and goods, who live at the navel of the earth.
en.B: in order to seize plunder and loot, to turn your hand against the resettled ruins and against the people gathered from the nations, who have gained livestock and goods and who live at the center of the world.
en.R: You will want to rob them and take their things. You will want to attack the towns that were in ruins but now have people living in them. Those people were gathered from the nations. They now have cattle and other things, and they live at the center of the world.

pt.L: para saquear saque e tomar despojo, para voltar a tua mão contra as ruínas [agora] habitadas, e contra um povo reunido das nações, que adquire gado e bens, que habita no umbigo da terra.
pt.B: para tomar saque e despojo, para voltar a tua mão contra as ruínas repovoadas e contra o povo reunido das nações, que ganhou gado e bens e que vive no centro do mundo.
pt.R: Tu vais querer roubá-los e levar as coisas deles. Vais querer atacar as cidades que estavam em ruínas mas agora têm gente morando nelas. Aquele povo foi reunido das nações. Agora eles têm gado e outros bens e vivem no centro do mundo.

decisions.choice: the navel of the earth: the center of the world
decisions.reason: The word *tabbur* is used only here and in Judges 9:37. It is often taken as "navel", the center of the earth, as Jerusalem is set "in the center of the nations" in 5:5. Others take it as "the high ground", the mountain heights of Israel.

decisions.choice: to turn your hand: Gog's speech turns into the LORD's address
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves from Gog's words ("I will go up") to "your hand", as the LORD speaks to Gog again. Literal and Balanced follow the change.

decisions.choice: You will want to rob them (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the purpose as Gog's wish, and makes the long sentence several short ones. "Center of the world" follows the first reading in m1.

source.text: שְׁבָ֡א וּ֠דְדָן וְסֹחֲרֵ֨י תַרְשִׁ֤ישׁ וְכָל־כְּפִרֶ֨יהָ֙ יֹאמְר֣וּ לְךָ֔ הֲלִשְׁלֹ֤ל שָׁלָל֙ אַתָּ֣ה בָ֔א הֲלָבֹ֥ז בַּ֖ז הִקְהַ֣לְתָּ קְהָלֶ֑ךָ לָשֵׂ֣את׀כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֗ב לָקַ֨חַת֙ מִקְנֶ֣ה וְקִנְיָ֔ן לִשְׁלֹ֖ל שָׁלָ֥ל גָּדֽוֹל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Sheba and Dedan and [the] traders of Tarshish and all its young lions will say to you: To plunder plunder are you coming? To seize spoil have you assembled your company, to carry off silver and gold, to take livestock and goods, to plunder great plunder?

en.L: Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish and all its young lions will say to you, "Have you come to take plunder? Have you assembled your company to seize spoil, to carry off silver and gold, to take away livestock and goods, to seize great plunder?"
en.B: Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish with all its young lions will ask you, "Have you come to take plunder? Have you gathered your army to carry off loot, to take away silver and gold, livestock and goods, and to seize a great haul?"
en.R: Sheba, Dedan, the traders of Tarshish and all its leaders will ask you, "Did you come here to rob? Did you bring your army to steal silver and gold, cattle and other things, and to take great riches?"

pt.L: Sabá e Dedã e os mercadores de Társis e todos os seus leões novos te dirão: "É para saquear saque que vens? É para tomar despojo que reuniste a tua multidão, para levar prata e ouro, para tomar gado e bens, para saquear um grande saque?"
pt.B: Sabá e Dedã e os mercadores de Társis, com todos os seus leões novos, te perguntarão: "Vieste para tomar saque? Reuniste o teu exército para levar despojos, para carregar prata e ouro, gado e bens, e para fazer uma grande pilhagem?"
pt.R: Sabá, Dedã, os comerciantes de Társis e todos os seus líderes vão te perguntar: "Tu vieste aqui para roubar? Trouxeste o teu exército para levar prata e ouro, gado e outros bens, e para tomar grandes riquezas?"

decisions.choice: Sheba, Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish: the great traders
decisions.reason: Sheba and Dedan were trading peoples of Arabia, and Tarshish a port in the far west, probably in Spain (27:12, 20-22). They ask about the invasion as merchants, perhaps hoping to buy the plunder.

decisions.choice: its young lions: its leaders, or its villages
decisions.reason: Young lions often stand for princes or warriors (19:2-6; 32:2). With other vowels the word could mean "its villages", and the Septuagint reads differently.

decisions.choice: all its leaders (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the picture (m2). The merchants' question takes double quotation marks.

decisions.choice: tu, from the merchants to Gog
decisions.reason: The merchants speak to Gog with "tu" too, keeping the address of the LORD's oracle in which their words are quoted; a change to "você" inside the oracle would read as a different scene.

source.text: לָכֵן֙ הִנָּבֵ֣א בֶן־אָדָ֔ם וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ לְג֔וֹג כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הֲל֣וֹא׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא בְּשֶׁ֨בֶת עַמִּ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל לָבֶ֖טַח תֵּדָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Will you not, on that day, when my people Israel dwell securely, know [it]?

en.L: Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: On that day, when {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel are living securely, will you not know [it]?
en.B: Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: On that day, when {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel are living in safety, will you not take notice?
en.R: So prophesy, son of man. Tell Gog, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: At that time {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel will be living in safety, and you will know it.

pt.L: Por isso profetiza, filho do homem, e dize a Gogue: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Naquele dia, quando o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo Israel estiver habitando em segurança, não o saberás?
pt.B: Por isso, profetiza, filho do homem, e dize a Gogue: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Naquele dia, quando o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo Israel estiver vivendo em segurança, não vais perceber isso?
pt.R: Por isso, profetiza, filho do homem. Dize a Gogue: É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz: Naquele tempo o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo Israel vai estar vivendo em segurança, e tu vais saber disso.

decisions.choice: will you not know it: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew asks, "will you not know?", that is, Gog will notice that Israel is defenseless and seize the chance. The Septuagint reads "will you not rouse yourself?", which needs a change of one letter. The standard Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. Readable turns the question into a statement, which says the same thing.

source.text: וּבָ֤אתָ מִמְּקֽוֹמְךָ֙ מִיַּרְכְּתֵ֣י צָפ֔וֹן אַתָּ֕ה וְעַמִּ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים אִתָּ֑ךְ רֹכְבֵ֤י סוּסִים֙ כֻּלָּ֔ם קָהָ֥ל גָּד֖וֹל וְחַ֥יִל רָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will come from your place, from [the] remotest parts of [the] north, you and many peoples with you, riders on horses all of them, a great company and a mighty army.

en.L: And you will come from your place out of the remotest parts of the north, you and many peoples with you, riders on horses all of them, a great assembly and a mighty army.
en.B: You will come from your home in the far north, you and many nations with you, all of them on horseback, a great horde and a mighty army.
en.R: You will come from your home in the far north. Many nations will come with you, all of them riding horses. It will be a huge and powerful army.

pt.L: E virás do teu lugar, dos confins do norte, tu e muitos povos contigo, todos eles montados em cavalos, uma grande multidão e um exército poderoso.
pt.B: Virás da tua terra, no extremo norte, tu e muitas nações contigo, todos montados a cavalo, uma grande multidão e um exército poderoso.
pt.R: Tu virás da tua terra, no extremo norte. Muitas nações virão contigo, todos montados a cavalo. Será um exército enorme e poderoso.

decisions.choice: the remotest parts of the north
decisions.reason: See verse 6.

source.text: וְעָלִ֨יתָ֙ עַל־עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֶּֽעָנָ֖ן לְכַסּ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ בְּאַחֲרִ֨ית הַיָּמִ֜ים תִּֽהְיֶ֗ה וַהֲבִאוֹתִ֨יךָ֙ עַל־אַרְצִ֔י לְמַעַן֩ דַּ֨עַת הַגּוֹיִ֜ם אֹתִ֗י בְּהִקָּדְשִׁ֥י בְךָ֛ לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם גּֽוֹג׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you will come up against my people Israel like a cloud to cover the land. In the latter days it will be, and I will bring you against my land, so that the nations may know me, when I show myself holy through you before their eyes, Gog.

en.L: And you will come up against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel like a cloud to cover the land. In the latter days it will be, and I will bring you upon {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land, in order that the nations may know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} when through you, Gog, I show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} holy before their eyes.
en.B: Like a cloud covering the land, you will advance on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. In the latter days I will bring you against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land, Gog, so that the nations come to know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} when through you I show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} holy before their eyes.
en.R: You will attack {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel. You will cover the land like a cloud. In the days to come, Gog, I will bring you against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land. Then the nations will know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} when they see how I show that I am holy by what I do to you.

pt.L: E subirás contra o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo Israel como uma nuvem para cobrir a terra. Nos últimos dias isso acontecerá, e eu te trarei contra a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} terra, para que as nações {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conheçam, quando por meio de ti, ó Gogue, eu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} mostrar santo diante dos olhos delas.
pt.B: Como uma nuvem que cobre a terra, avançarás contra o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo Israel. Nos últimos dias eu te trarei contra a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} terra, Gogue, para que as nações {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conheçam, quando por meio de ti eu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} mostrar santo diante dos olhos delas.
pt.R: Tu vais atacar o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo Israel. Vais cobrir a terra como uma nuvem. Nos dias que virão, Gogue, eu vou te trazer contra a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} terra. Então as nações vão {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conhecer, quando virem como eu mostro que sou santo pelo que faço contigo.

decisions.choice: in the latter days: the time ahead
decisions.reason: See verse 8.

decisions.choice: so that the nations may know me when I show myself holy through you
decisions.reason: The purpose of Gog's coming is that the nations should know the LORD. He showed his holiness to the nations by restoring Israel (36:23); he will show it again by defeating Gog (verse 23; 39:7, 21-27).

decisions.choice: my land: the land belongs to the LORD
decisions.reason: Gog attacks the LORD's own land (36:5).

decisions.choice: Gog (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew ends the verse with "O Gog". Each level moves the name to where it reads naturally in English.

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הַֽאַתָּה־ה֨וּא אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֜רְתִּי בְּיָמִ֣ים קַדְמוֹנִ֗ים בְּיַד֙ עֲבָדַי֙ נְבִיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַֽנִּבְּאִ֛ים בַּיָּמִ֥ים הָהֵ֖ם שָׁנִ֑ים לְהָבִ֥יא אֹתְךָ֖ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Are you he of whom I spoke in former days by the hand of my servants the prophets of Israel, who prophesied in those days for years that I would bring you against them?

en.L: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Are you the one of whom I spoke in former days by the hand of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets of Israel, who in those days prophesied, [for] years, that I would bring you upon them?
en.B: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Are you not the one I spoke about in days long past through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets of Israel? In those days they prophesied for years that I would bring you against them.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Long ago I spoke about you through {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants, the prophets of Israel. For years they prophesied that I would bring you against Israel. You are the one they spoke about.

pt.L: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: És tu aquele de quem falei nos dias antigos por meio dos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} servos, os profetas de Israel, que naqueles dias profetizaram, [por] anos, que eu te traria contra eles?
pt.B: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}: Não és tu aquele de quem falei em tempos passados por meio dos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} servos, os profetas de Israel? Naqueles dias, eles profetizaram durante anos que eu te traria contra eles.
pt.R: É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz: Há muito tempo falei de ti por meio dos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} servos, os profetas de Israel. Durante anos eles profetizaram que eu te traria contra Israel. Tu és aquele de quem eles falavam.

decisions.choice: are you he of whom I spoke: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew asks, "Are you he ...?" It means that Gog is the enemy the earlier prophets foretold. The Septuagint and other versions read it as a statement: "You are the one".

decisions.choice: my servants the prophets: earlier prophecies of a northern enemy
decisions.reason: No earlier prophet names Gog, but Jeremiah speaks of a foe from the north (Jeremiah 4-6), and Isaiah, Joel and Zephaniah of nations that will come against Zion and be judged (Isaiah 29:5-8; Joel 4:2, 9-14; Zephaniah 3:8). Gog gathers these prophecies into one figure.

decisions.choice: servants (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The word *'eved* for the prophets is "servants" at every level, as in the published prophets (Jeremiah 7:25; Amos 3:7). Readable gives the question as the statement it implies (m1), and says "Israel" for "them".

source.text: וְהָיָ֣ה׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא בְּי֨וֹם בּ֥וֹא גוֹג֙ עַל־אַדְמַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה תַּעֲלֶ֥ה חֲמָתִ֖י בְּאַפִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be on that day, on the day Gog comes against [the] land of Israel, declares [the] Lord Yahweh, my wrath will rise up in my anger.

en.L: And it will come about on that day, on the day of Gog's coming against the land of Israel, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, [that] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will mount up in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger.
en.B: But on that day, when Gog attacks the land of Israel, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath will blaze up in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger.
en.R: When Gog attacks the land of Israel, I will become very angry, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: E acontecerá naquele dia, no dia da vinda de Gogue contra a terra de Israel, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, [que] o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} furor subirá na {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} ira.
pt.B: Mas naquele dia, quando Gogue atacar a terra de Israel, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} furor se inflamará na {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} ira.
pt.R: Quando Gogue atacar a terra de Israel, eu vou ficar muito irado, diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: my wrath will rise up in my nostrils: my anger will blaze
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "my wrath will come up in my nose"; the word for anger is the word for nose, from the hard breathing of rage (compare Psalm 18:9).

decisions.choice: wrath (L, B); angry (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *chemah*. Readable joins the two words for anger.

decisions.choice: furor (L, B); muito irado (R)
decisions.reason: Chemah is "furor" and 'aph "ira" at Literal and Balanced, two words for the LORD's anger as the English keeps "wrath" and "anger"; Readable joins them, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וּבְקִנְאָתִ֥י בְאֵשׁ־עֶבְרָתִ֖י דִּבַּ֑רְתִּי אִם־לֹ֣א׀בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶה֙ רַ֣עַשׁ גָּד֔וֹל עַ֖ל אַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And in my jealousy, in the fire of my wrath, I have spoken: surely on that day there will be a great earthquake in [the] land of Israel.

en.L: For I have spoken in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} jealousy, in the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath: surely in that day a great shaking will come upon the land of Israel.
en.B: In {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} jealousy and in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blazing wrath I declare that a great earthquake will strike the land of Israel on that day.
en.R: I am jealous for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land, and I am burning with anger. So I promise you that at that time there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel.

pt.L: Pois falei no {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} zelo, no fogo do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} furor: certamente naquele dia haverá um grande tremor sobre a terra de Israel.
pt.B: No {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} zelo e no fogo do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} furor eu declaro que naquele dia um grande terremoto atingirá a terra de Israel.
pt.R: Eu tenho zelo pela {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} terra e estou ardendo de ira. Por isso eu prometo a ti que naquele tempo haverá um grande terremoto na terra de Israel.

decisions.choice: a great earthquake: the shaking of the whole creation
decisions.reason: The word *ra'ash* (37:7) means a shaking. Here it is an earthquake that shakes the whole creation (verse 20), as when the LORD comes in judgment (Joel 4:16; Haggai 2:6; Revelation 16:18).

decisions.choice: shaking (L); earthquake (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal says "shaking", the plain sense of the word; Balanced and Readable say "earthquake", which is what it is here. Readable says "jealous for my land" for the LORD's zeal (36:5).

decisions.choice: zelo; tremor (L); terremoto (B, R)
decisions.reason: Qin'ah is the LORD's jealous zeal for what is his; "zelo" says that in Portuguese without the pettiness that "ciúme" carries in everyday speech. Literal says "tremor", the plain sense of ra'ash (m1, the "estalar" of 37:7); Balanced and Readable say "terremoto", as the English.

source.text: וְרָעֲשׁ֣וּ מִפָּנַ֡י דְּגֵ֣י הַיָּם֩ וְע֨וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֜יִם וְחַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה וְכָל־הָרֶ֨מֶשׂ֙ הָרֹמֵ֣שׂ עַל־הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה וְכֹל֙ הָֽאָדָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הָאֲדָמָ֑ה וְנֶהֶרְס֣וּ הֶהָרִ֗ים וְנָֽפְלוּ֙ הַמַּדְרֵג֔וֹת וְכָל־חוֹמָ֖ה לָאָ֥רֶץ תִּפּֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will tremble before me: the fish of the sea and the birds of the heavens and the animals of the field and every creeping thing that creeps on the ground and all humankind that [is] on the face of the ground; and the mountains will be thrown down, and the steep places will fall, and every wall will fall to the ground.

en.L: And before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the fish of the sea and the birds of the sky and the animals of the field will quake, and every creeping thing that creeps on the ground, and all the people who [are] on the face of the earth; and the mountains will be thrown down, and the cliffs will fall, and every wall will fall to the ground.
en.B: The fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the wild animals, every creature that creeps along the ground, and all the people on the face of the earth will quake before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}}. The mountains will be overturned, the cliffs will collapse, and every wall will crumble to the ground.
en.R: Fish, birds, wild animals, creatures that crawl on the ground and all the people in the world will shake with fear in front of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. The mountains will fall down, the cliffs will crash, and every wall will fall to the ground.

pt.L: E tremerão diante de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} os peixes do mar, e as aves do céu, e os animais do campo, e todo réptil que rasteja sobre o chão, e todas as pessoas que [estão] sobre a face da terra; e os montes serão derrubados, e os penhascos cairão, e todo muro cairá por terra.
pt.B: Os peixes do mar, as aves do céu, os animais selvagens, todos os seres que rastejam pelo chão e todas as pessoas que estão sobre a face da terra tremerão diante de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. Os montes serão derrubados, os penhascos desabarão, e todo muro desmoronará por terra.
pt.R: Os peixes, as aves, os animais selvagens, os bichos que se arrastam no chão e todas as pessoas do mundo vão tremer de medo diante de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}. Os montes vão desabar, os penhascos vão cair, e todo muro vai ruir até o chão.

decisions.choice: fish, birds, animals, creeping things and people: the creatures of Genesis 1
decisions.reason: The list follows the order of creation in Genesis 1:26-28. The whole created world trembles before the LORD's coming (compare Hosea 4:3; Zephaniah 1:3).

decisions.choice: the steep places: the terraces or cliffs
decisions.reason: The word means steep places, perhaps the terraced hillsides on which crops were grown, or cliffs.

decisions.choice: all the people (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The word *ha'adam* means humankind; "people" needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: todas as pessoas, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Ha'adam is humankind; "todas as pessoas" already includes everyone, as the English "all the people" needs no setting.

source.text: וְקָרָ֨אתִי עָלָ֤יו לְכָל־הָרַי֙ חֶ֔רֶב נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה חֶ֥רֶב אִ֖ישׁ בְּאָחִ֥יו תִּֽהְיֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will call against him to all my mountains a sword, declares [the] Lord Yahweh; [the] sword of each will be against his brother.

en.L: And I will summon a sword against him on all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mountains, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}; every man's sword will be against his brother.
en.B: On all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mountains I will call for a sword against Gog, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. Every soldier's sword will be turned against his comrade.
en.R: I will send war against Gog on all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mountains, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. His soldiers will fight and kill one another.

pt.L: E chamarei contra ele a espada sobre todos os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} montes, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}; a espada de cada um será contra o seu irmão.
pt.B: Sobre todos os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} montes chamarei a espada contra Gogue, declara o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}. A espada de cada soldado se voltará contra o seu companheiro.
pt.R: Vou mandar a guerra contra Gogue em todos os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} montes, diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}. Os soldados dele vão lutar e matar uns aos outros.

decisions.choice: each one's sword against his brother: the enemy destroys itself
decisions.reason: In the holy wars of Israel the LORD threw the enemy into panic, so that they killed one another (Judges 7:22; 1 Samuel 14:20; 2 Chronicles 20:23; Haggai 2:22).

decisions.choice: to all my mountains a sword: the text may be damaged
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is awkward. The Septuagint reads "every terror" in place of "to all my mountains a sword". The standard Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: Gog (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Gog for "him". The soldiers are men, so the verse takes no gender setting.

source.text: וְנִשְׁפַּטְתִּ֥י אִתּ֖וֹ בְּדֶ֣בֶר וּבְדָ֑ם וְגֶ֣שֶׁם שׁוֹטֵף֩ וְאַבְנֵ֨י אֶלְגָּבִ֜ישׁ אֵ֣שׁ וְגָפְרִ֗ית אַמְטִ֤יר עָלָיו֙ וְעַל־אֲגַפָּ֔יו וְעַל־עַמִּ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will enter into judgment with him by pestilence and by blood; and overflowing rain and hailstones, fire and sulfur I will rain on him and on his troops and on the many peoples who [are] with him.

en.L: And I will go to judgment with him, with pestilence and with blood; and torrential rain and hailstones, fire and sulfur, I will rain down on him and on his troops and on the many peoples who [are] with him.
en.B: I will bring him to judgment with plague and bloodshed. I will pour down on him, on his troops and on the many peoples with him torrents of rain, hailstones, fire and burning sulfur.
en.R: I will punish him with disease and death. I will send heavy rain, hail, fire and burning sulfur down on him and his army and on the many nations with him.

pt.L: E entrarei em juízo com ele, com peste e com sangue; e chuva torrencial e pedras de granizo, fogo e enxofre farei chover sobre ele e sobre as suas tropas e sobre os muitos povos que [estão] com ele.
pt.B: Eu o levarei a juízo com peste e derramamento de sangue. Farei cair sobre ele, sobre as suas tropas e sobre os muitos povos que estão com ele chuvas torrenciais, pedras de granizo, fogo e enxofre ardente.
pt.R: Vou castigá-lo com doença e morte. Vou mandar chuva forte, granizo, fogo e enxofre ardente sobre ele, sobre o seu exército e sobre as muitas nações que estão com ele.

decisions.choice: fire and sulfur rained down: Genesis 19:24
decisions.reason: The LORD rained fire and sulfur on Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:24; Psalm 11:6), and sent hail on Egypt (Exodus 9:23-24) and on the Amorites (Joshua 10:11). Revelation 20:9 takes up the fire that comes down on Gog and Magog, and Revelation 20:10 the lake of fire and sulfur.

decisions.choice: I will enter into judgment with him: I will judge him
decisions.reason: The verb means to go to law with someone, to bring them to judgment (17:20; 20:35-36).

decisions.choice: pestilence, blood (L); plague, bloodshed (B); disease, death (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *deber* in Ezekiel. Readable says "death" for "blood".

decisions.choice: peste, sangue (L); peste, derramamento de sangue (B); doença, morte (R)
decisions.reason: Deber as the Ezekiel notes set it ("peste" at Literal and Balanced, "doença" at Readable), and "enxofre", the word of Genesis 19:24 (m1).

source.text: וְהִתְגַּדִּלְתִּי֙ וְהִתְקַדִּשְׁתִּ֔י וְנ֣וֹדַעְתִּ֔י לְעֵינֵ֖י גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֑ים וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will show myself great and show myself holy, and I will make myself known before [the] eyes of many nations; and they will know that I [am] Yahweh.

en.L: And I will show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} great and show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} holy, and make {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} known before the eyes of many nations; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: So I will show {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} great and holy, and I will make {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} known before many nations. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: In this way I will show many nations how great and holy I am. I will show them who I am, and they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} engrandecerei e {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} santificarei, e {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} farei conhecer diante dos olhos de muitas nações; e saberão que eu [sou] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Assim mostrarei a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} grandeza e a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} santidade, e {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} farei conhecer diante de muitas nações. Então saberão que eu sou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Desse modo, vou mostrar a muitas nações como sou grande e santo. Vou mostrar a elas quem eu sou, e elas saberão que eu sou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: I will show myself great and holy and make myself known: the purpose of the battle
decisions.reason: The three verbs sum up why the LORD brings Gog: so that the nations will know the greatness and holiness of the LORD (verse 16; 36:23).

decisions.choice: the refrain as settled
decisions.reason: The settled wording of the refrain.

decisions.choice: E me engrandecerei e me santificarei
decisions.reason: A Portuguese sentence may not open with an unstressed pronoun in written style; Literal keeps the opening "E", so the reflexive verbs can stand as the Hebrew has them, each with its deity_pronoun span like the English "myself".
